issue_context.title: AIP 75 || Task name showing as __main__ instead of function name
issue_context.body: ### Apache Airflow version main (development) ### If "Other Airflow 2 version" selected, which one? _No response_ ### What happened? Task name is showing `__main__` instead it should show as function name ### What you think should happen instead? ### How to reproduce 1. Use below DAG and check task name ``` from airflow.sdk.definitions.asset.decorators import asset @asset(schedule=None,uri="s3://bucket/asset1_producer") def raw_customers(): print("Retrieving raw customer data") @asset(schedule=raw_customers) def stg_customers(): print("Transforming raw customer data") ``` ### Operating System Linux ### Versions of Apache Airflow Providers _No response_ ### Deployment Other ### Deployment details _No response_ ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Are you willing to submit PR? - [ ] Yes I am willing to submit a PR! ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

review_comments:
I feel we probably should use 
```suggestion
            task_id=definition.name,
```
instead?

So that means assent name becomes the task_id, so its more or like question now , which one is better serves here. If user removes the asset name, can we consider that asset is invalid? in this case a new task will appear with the function name. as there is no asset name it picks up function name as asset name.

>  If user removes the asset name, can we consider that asset is invalid

it depends. The asset might still exist elsewhere. So I guess the answer to this one is no.

> in this case a new task will appear with the function name. as there is no asset name it picks up function name as asset name.

yep, just like the dag itself
